source.title: MI-MIDI 2: From Observation to Control with Sparse Autoencoders in Text-to-MIDI Generation

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study applies SAE feature analysis and steering in symbolic text-to-MIDI models, a new setting for indirect evidence about SAE features in real models. It also checks cross-dictionary recurrence for one feature, but does not test superposition geometry.
record.gate_note: Rows cover SAE reconstruction, feature steering, and cross-dictionary recurrence that bear on indirect SAE-feature evidence or feature stability. The paper does not measure feature overlap, near-orthogonal geometry, neuron polysemanticity, or feature dimensionality. Observational metric associations and description-recognition results are not themselves evidence that SAE features are the model’s canonical units; cited findings from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study trains TopK SAEs on two text-to-MIDI transformers, one Llama-3.2-1B-based. It reports reconstruction and loss recovery, which is indirect evidence that sparse dictionary features exist (V4), and cross-dictionary recurrence of features (V5). These are results in a new setting. Most of the paper asks whether observational interpretations of SAE features predict steering. That is a related but different construct, so it is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that controlled observational evidence identifies some steerable SAE features: the synth-lead feature was confirmed and replicated, and density-adjusted selections showed a small family shift. Raw correlations and most descriptions did not predict steering, and single-feature recurrence does not establish whole-dictionary stability.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains TopK SAE dictionaries on residual states in text-to-MIDI models and steers their decoder directions, with baseline and matched-random controls. It does not reproduce Toy Models of Superposition or measure superposition geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: Feature-selection route and steering target matter: the density-adjusted family showed a small positive shift at P90 but not P50; raw-correlation families showed no reliable shift across P50, P75, and P90. Results also differed by candidate feature and program.

fits_no_version.finding: Whether observational evidence about SAE features predicts their steering effect depends on the selection route. The density-adjusted family shows +0.17 SD vs random at P90. Raw-correlation families show no shift. The program screen is inconsistent, and blinded description ratings show no pooled advantage.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Observational interpretations of SAE features (correlations, descriptions) reliably predict the features' causal steering effects.

record.problems: Each final dictionary is a single training run; broad screens use only eight or ten prompts per feature and one random direction per candidate. Family-level analyses were specified after the screens, and some sensitivity estimates are affected by excluded bootstrap draws. The LLM reviewer had no recorded sampling settings, wrote descriptions and made recognition choices in the same call, and saw instrument names and summary statistics. The synth-lead endpoint measures MIDI program number rather than perceived timbre. The study does not establish stability of whole dictionaries.
record.rows_left_out: No intervention-level per-feature metric rows or full candidate-level program rows are reproduced; the paper reports no primary per-feature rejection in these exploratory screens and presents the family-level results and selected candidate effects used here. Observational correlations and description recognition are not treated as tests of canonical feature identity.

untested.parts: No toy models, feature geometry, near-orthogonality or sparsity transition.
No test of capacity competition or dedicated dimensions for important features.
No analysis of the causes of neuron polysemanticity.
Does not test whether features are spread across neurons. Setting is music transformers rather than language LLMs. Loss recovery is reported for only 2 of 8 dictionaries.
Completeness and canonicity are not tested. Stability is checked only for L13 of text2midi, and there is no seed-repeat of the final dictionaries.
No comparison of 1-D directions with multidimensional features.

missing.what: Fraction of variance unexplained for all eight final dictionaries: 0.03–0.18 in text2midi and 0.25–0.44 in MIDI-LLM. This shows substantial residual variance in the larger model.
Features selected on unprompted excerpts rarely fire during prompted generation: 18 of 22 MIDI-LLM density-adjusted features never fire at baseline.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4 labels for the steering families (supports for r6, limits_scope for r7–r13) were removed. Those rows test interpretation-to-control, and V4 makes no claim about steerability. Only the reconstruction rows and the confirmed causal feature are linked to V4. The setting is music transformers; MIDI-LLM is Llama-3.2-1B-based, so the language-LLM generalization is indirect.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test storage of more sparse features than dimensions, overlap geometry, near-orthogonality, or sparsity-dependent transitions.
Does not test whether polysemantic neurons result from capacity competition or whether important features get dedicated dimensions.
Does not test alternative causes of polysemantic neurons or whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.

Tests SAE dictionaries and feature interventions in two text-to-MIDI models, not whether LLM features are generally spread across neurons or whether the learned features are complete recoveries of the models’ underlying features.

Checks cross-dictionary recurrence for the synth-lead feature and reports matching rates for final text2midi L13 features. Does not establish completeness, canonical status, or broad stability across features, models, and training runs.
Uses unit decoder directions but does not compare one-dimensional directions with multidimensional feature representations.

rows.subject: text2midi L13 f3340
rows.operation_detail: Added the SAE decoder direction to generation at target P90; compared program-81 presence with baseline and matched random-direction generation.
rows.measure: Outputs containing at least one non-drum program-81 note
rows.value: Feature direction: 14 of 20; random direction: 1 of 20
rows.uncertainty: Lift over random: 65 percentage points [45, 85]; exact one-sided p = 0.000122
rows.note: The confirmation was prespecified and passed the four stated success criteria.
rows.check: Keep, but weakly linked. It shows one recovered SAE direction causally controls program choice (14/20 vs 1/20 random). It does not show that features are spread across neurons.

rows.subject: text2midi L13 f3340
rows.operation_detail: Added the SAE decoder direction at P90 and measured program-81 presence on a disjoint prompt set.
rows.measure: Outputs containing at least one non-drum program-81 note
rows.value: Feature direction: 6 of 10; random direction: 0 of 10
rows.uncertainty: Lift over random: 60 percentage points [30, 90]; exact one-sided p = 0.015625
rows.note: The paper reports this as replication of the confirmation.
rows.check: Same as r3: a replication on disjoint prompts (6/10 vs 0/10). Weak link to V4.

rows.subject: text2midi and MIDI-LLM; 42 density-adjusted feature hypotheses across 21 SAEs
rows.operation_detail: Steered with selected SAE decoder directions and averaged metric effects across the feature family, oriented by each observational correlation.

conditions.value: 8 new prompts per feature; shared across features

rows.measure: Mean oriented target-metric effect in baseline standard deviations, feature minus random direction
rows.baseline: Random direction reference; mean effect +0.02 SD [−0.09, +0.12] relative to baseline
rows.note: The authors report the detectable positive family shift at P90, not P50.
rows.check: This tests whether density-adjusted correlation selection predicts steering, not whether sparse features exist. The baseline field repeats the value (+0.02) instead of giving the random-direction reference.

rows.subject: text2midi and MIDI-LLM; 42 density-adjusted feature hypotheses across 21 SAEs
rows.operation_detail: Steered with selected SAE decoder directions and averaged metric effects across the feature family, oriented by each density-adjusted correlation.

conditions.value: 8 new prompts per feature; shared across features

rows.measure: Mean oriented target-metric effect in baseline standard deviations, feature minus random direction
rows.baseline: Random direction: +0.01 SD [−0.15, +0.19] relative to baseline
rows.uncertainty: 95% prompt-resampling interval; feature versus baseline +0.18 SD [−0.04, +0.37]
rows.note: A small positive family-level shift; 27 of 42 oriented effects were positive. The effect relative to baseline has an interval including zero.
rows.check: Measures whether correlation-selected features steer their target metric, which is an interpretation-to-control question. V4 says nothing about steerability, so this row neither supports nor limits it.

rows.subject: text2midi and MIDI-LLM; 24 raw-correlation metric hypotheses across 7 SAEs
rows.operation_detail: Steered with features selected by raw metric correlations and averaged target-metric effects across the family.
rows.measure: Mean oriented target-metric effect in baseline standard deviations, feature minus random direction
rows.note: The paper reports no family-level shift for features selected by raw correlations.
rows.check: Tests a feature-selection route (raw correlation) for steering, not the existence of SAE-recoverable features.

rows.subject: text2midi and MIDI-LLM; 24 raw-correlation metric hypotheses across 7 SAEs
rows.operation_detail: Steered with features selected by raw metric correlations and averaged target-metric effects across the family.
rows.measure: Mean oriented target-metric effect in baseline standard deviations, feature minus random direction
rows.note: The interval is wide and includes zero; the paper reports no family-level shift for raw-correlation-selected features.

rows.subject: text2midi and MIDI-LLM; 24 raw-correlation metric hypotheses across 7 SAEs
rows.operation_detail: Steered with features selected by raw metric correlations and averaged target-metric effects across the family.
rows.measure: Mean oriented target-metric effect in baseline standard deviations, feature minus random direction
rows.note: Only 8 of 24 effects had the predicted sign; the authors report no family-level shift.

rows.subject: text2midi and MIDI-LLM; 27 program-feature hypotheses
rows.operation_detail: Steered with SAE features selected from shared instrument programs and counted program-positive outputs.
rows.value: Feature direction produced more program-positive outputs for 10 of 27 features and fewer for 10 of 27
rows.uncertainty: Per-feature exact tests; no primary per-feature rejection at q < 0.05
rows.note: The reported family result is inconsistent rather than a general increase in target-program presence.
rows.check: A program-feature steering screen, so the interpretation-to-control construct, not V4. There were 10 more vs 10 fewer of 27, and no per-feature rejection.

rows.subject: text2midi and MIDI-LLM; 10 program features with programs absent from all baselines
rows.operation_detail: Compared program presence under feature-direction and matched random-direction steering for the subset whose target program was absent from all baseline outputs.

conditions.value: 10 features with target program absent from all baseline outputs

rows.measure: Number of features whose target program was introduced
rows.baseline: Random direction introduced programs for 1 of 10 features
rows.value: Feature direction introduced programs for 6 of 10 features
rows.note: Exploratory subset comparison; not a consistent result across all 27 program features.
rows.check: An exploratory subset of a steering screen, not V4.

rows.subject: text2midi L16 f995
rows.operation_detail: Steered the SAE feature and measured Electric Piano 1 (program 4) presence and note share.
rows.measure: Outputs containing the target program; target-program share of non-drum notes
rows.baseline: Program present in 1 of 10 baseline outputs; note-share comparison is against random direction
rows.value: Program present in 5 of 10 feature outputs and 1 of 10 random outputs; note share increased by 17.4 percentage points over random
rows.note: The note-share increase was concentrated in four prompts; the per-feature exploratory screen had no primary rejection at q < 0.05.
rows.check: A single-feature exploratory steering effect, not V4.

rows.subject: text2midi and MIDI-LLM; 12 audit-passing description candidates
rows.operation_detail: A blinded LLM reviewer rated feature-direction and random-direction outputs against fixed feature descriptions.
rows.note: The pooled interval includes zero. The synth-lead feature had the largest individual difference, but without it the subset difference was −0.036 [−0.400, 0.291].
rows.check: Blinded LLM ratings of description match under steering test the validity of descriptions, not V4.

rows.measure: Feature activation correlation with matched dictionary feature

rows.operation_detail: Matched the synth-lead feature to the most correlated feature in an independently trained dictionary with a different expansion factor.

rows.subject: text2midi L13 final-dictionary features
rows.operation_detail: Measured the proportion of final L13 features with a cross-dictionary match of r ≥ 0.8 on both discovery and validation splits.

conditions.value: Earlier L13 dictionary with same expansion factor

rows.measure: Share of final L13 features meeting r ≥ 0.8 on both splits
rows.note: The corresponding proportion for the dictionary with expansion factor 4 was 25.6%; the authors caution that one feature match does not establish stability of whole dictionaries.
rows.check: The value merges two dictionaries: 35.2% (same EF) and 25.6% (EF 4) of final L13 features match at r≥0.8 on both splits. Better as two rows. These are the main stability numbers, not merely a comparator.
